about: Spanish verb tables (docs/content-plan.md §4.1). Page /grammar/verbs, search hits and worksheets via src/lib/verbtabellen.js; the generator is src/lib/verbtabellenCore.js. A tense is a comma list of six forms: yo, tú, él/ella/usted, nosotros/as, vosotros/as, ellos/ellas/ustedes. `regular: true` stores no forms. Other verbs store only what can't be derived: praes (presente), praet (indefinido), imperf (imperfecto), fut (futuro), cond (condicional, else from fut), subj (presente de subjuntivo, else from the yo form), subjImpf (imperfecto de subjuntivo in -ra, else from the indefinido; -se is generated), imp (imperativo afirmativo, – for yo; the negative is no + subj), ger, p2. Compound tenses are haber + p2. A pronominal verb stores forms without the pronoun; the generator adds it, except in `imp`, which it stores in full if at all. A pronominal verb inherits the stored tenses of its plain verb when that verb is in this file. Group ids are kept from the German tables: hilfsverb = ser, estar, haber, ir; modal = verb + infinitive; unregelmaessig = irregular; regelmaessig = regular; trennbar = reflexive and pronominal. `en` and `level` are this table's own, until the Spanish lexicon has the verb. pnpm check:verbtabellen checks the forms.

es419.note: In everyday speech Latin America uses ustedes, not vosotros: the ellos/ellas/ustedes form. Voseo (Argentina, etc.) isn't covered here.

groups.name: Regular verbs
groups.what: Take -ar, -er or -ir off the infinitive and add the endings. Most verbs work like this, and new verbs do too.
regel: Three patterns: *hablar – hablo, hablas, habla*; *comer – como, comes, come*; *vivir – vivo, vives, vive*. -er and -ir differ only in *comemos / vivimos*, *coméis / vivís* and the vosotros imperative.
The accent changes the word: *hablo* = I speak, *habló* = he or she spoke; *hable* = subjunctive or usted command, *hablé* = I spoke.

Spelling keeps the sound, so these forms are highlighted: *buscar – busqué*, *llegar – llegué*, *coger – cojo*. A vowel before the ending gives *leer – leyó, leyendo*, with an accent in *leíste, leído*.
Polite *usted* and *ustedes* use the third-person form: *¿Usted habla inglés? ¿Ustedes viven aquí?*
*vosotros* is the informal plural 'you' in most of Spain: *¿Habláis inglés?* In Latin America people say *ustedes*: *¿Hablan inglés?*
The imperfect subjunctive has two forms that mean the same: *hablara / hablase*. The *-ra* form is the more common one in speech.

groups.name: ser, estar, haber, ir
groups.what: The four verbs you need from day one. All four are irregular in the present, the indefinido and the subjunctive.
meaning: who or what something is: identity, origin, job, time
where something is, and how it is right now
builds the compound tenses; hay = there is
to go; ir a + infinitive = going to
regel: *ser* for what something is: *Soy enfermera. Es de Marruecos. Son las tres.*
*estar* for place and state: *Estoy en Madrid. La oficina está cerrada.*
*haber* + participle makes every compound tense, and the participle never changes: *he comido, habíamos salido.*
Use *hay*, not *ha*, for 'there is / there are': *Hay una farmacia aquí.* It stays the same for plurals: *hay dos.*
*ser* and *ir* share one indefinido, and the sentence tells you which is meant: *Fui médico* (I was a doctor). *Fui al médico* (I went to the doctor).

groups.name: Stem-changing verbs
groups.what: The stressed vowel of the stem changes: e → ie, o → ue, e → i. The endings stay regular.
regel: The change comes only where the stem is stressed: yo, tú, él and ellos. *pienso, piensas, piensa, piensan*, but *pensamos, pensáis*.
The present subjunctive follows the same shape: *piense, pienses*, but *pensemos, penséis*. The tú imperative too: *piensa, vuelve, pide.*

-ir verbs have one more change: e → i, o → u in él and ellos of the indefinido (and so in the whole imperfect subjunctive), in the gerund, and in nosotros and vosotros of the present subjunctive: *pidió, durmieron, sintiera, sintiendo, durmamos.*
*-ar* and *-er* stem-changers are regular in the indefinido: *pensé, pensó; volví, volvió.*
*jugar* is the only u → ue verb: *juego, juegas*. Spelling adds to the change: *jugué, empecé, sigo, elijo.*

groups.name: Irregular verbs
groups.what: Each has its own forms, shown highlighted, but they fall into groups you can learn together.
regel: Irregular yo in the present: *tengo, hago, pongo, salgo, digo, traigo, conozco, conduzco.* The whole present subjunctive comes from it: *tengo → tenga, hago → haga.*
A new stem in the indefinido, with no written accent: *tuve, hice, puse, dije, vine, traje*. Endings: *-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron* (*-eron* after j: *dijeron*).
A changed stem in the future, and the conditional shares it: *tendré, tendría; haré, haría; diré, diría; saldré, saldría.*
Short tú imperatives: *ten, ven, pon, sal, haz, di*, plus *ve* (ir) and *sé* (ser). The negative is regular: *no tengas, no hagas.*
Irregular participles to learn: *hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, escrito, abierto, roto, vuelto, muerto.*

groups.name: Verb + infinitive
groups.what: They say what is possible, wanted, necessary or usual. A second verb follows, in the infinitive.
regel: Most take the infinitive directly, with no preposition: *Puedo venir mañana. Quiero alquilar un piso.*
*no* goes first: *No puedo ir. No debes fumar aquí.*
Pronouns go before the first verb or on the end of the infinitive: *Lo quiero ver = Quiero verlo.*
*saber* for a skill, *poder* for what the situation allows: *Sé conducir, pero hoy no puedo.*
Obligation in everyday speech is *tener que*: *Tengo que pedir cita previa.* The conditional is polite: *¿Podría ayudarme?*

groups.name: Reflexive and pronominal verbs
groups.what: Verb + pronoun (me, te, se, nos, os, se). The pronoun changes with the person: me levanto a las siete, se levanta a las ocho.
regel: The pronoun comes before a conjugated verb: *me levanto, te llamas, nos hemos sentado.* In compound tenses it comes before *haber*.
It attaches to an affirmative imperative, and often an accent is needed: *levántate, siéntese.* In the negative it stays in front: *no te levantes.*
With an infinitive or gerund it can go in either place: *Me voy a duchar = Voy a ducharme. Me estoy vistiendo = Estoy vistiéndome.*
Before *-os*, the vosotros imperative drops its d: *levantaos, sentaos, vestíos*. *irse* is the exception and keeps it: *idos*.
The pronoun can change the meaning: *ir* = go, *irse* = leave; *poner* = put, *ponerse* = put on; *quedar* = meet, *quedarse* = stay.

verbs.note: The model for -ar verbs.
The model for -er verbs.
The model for -ir verbs.
Mostly in the third person, with a pronoun in front: me gusta el café, me gustan las tapas.
c → qu before e: busqué, busque. Works the same way: sacar, tocar, explicar.
g → gu before e: llegué, llegue. Works the same way: pagar, entregar.
A vowel before the ending: leíste, leyó, leyendo, leído. Works the same way: creer.
g → j before a and o: cojo, coja. Everyday Spain: coger el autobús.
